summary: Hyaluronidase is an enzyme used as an adjuvant (spreading) agent to increase the dispersion and absorption of subcutaneously administered fluids and drugs and to improve resorption of radiopaque agents in subcutaneous urography. It transiently breaks down hyaluronic acid in the ground substance of connective tissue. Off-label it is widely used to treat drug/contrast extravasation and to reverse hyaluronic acid dermal fillers. It must not be injected into infected or inflamed areas (risk of spreading infection) or applied to the cornea, and the main risk is hypersensitivity, including rare anaphylactoid reactions.
indications: Adjuvant in subcutaneous fluid administration for achieving hydration
To increase the dispersion and absorption of other injected drugs
Adjuvant in subcutaneous urography to improve resorption of radiopaque agents
Management of extravasation of certain agents (clinical/off-label use)

dosage.n: Rate/volume of fluid governed by patient age, weight and clinical condition; caution in young children

dosage.n: Used to speed absorption of co-administered agents

admin: Inspect parenteral product for particulate matter and discoloration before use
Use aseptic technique; for clysis, insert the needle with the tip free between skin and muscle and begin fluid which should flow without pain or lump
Do not inject into or around an infected or acutely inflamed area, and do not use to reduce swelling from bites or stings
Do not apply directly to the cornea
If administered intravenously the enzyme is rapidly inactivated (intended for local/subcutaneous use)
moa: Hyaluronidase is a dispersion (spreading) agent that hydrolyzes hyaluronic acid, the polysaccharide forming the intercellular ground substance of connective tissue. By temporarily depolymerizing hyaluronic acid it lowers the viscosity of this matrix and increases tissue permeability, allowing injected fluids and drugs to spread and be absorbed more rapidly. The effect is local and reversible, with the tissue barrier reconstituting within about 24 to 48 hours as hyaluronic acid is regenerated.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to hyaluronidase or any excipient in the formulation
relative: Injection into or around infected or acutely inflamed tissue
Use to reduce swelling of bites or stings
Areas with known malignancy (theoretical risk of spread)
monitor: Signs of hypersensitivity or anaphylactoid reaction
Local reactions and spread of any underlying infection
Fluid status when used to facilitate large-volume clysis

preg: There are no adequate, well-controlled studies of hyaluronidase in pregnant women; it should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether hyaluronidase is excreted in human milk; because brief local administration produces limited systemic exposure, the risk to a breastfed infant is likely low, but use caution.
renal: No specific renal dosage adjustment is described; the enzyme acts locally and is rapidly broken down.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dosage adjustment is described.

moderate: Local anesthetics (hyaluronidase speeds onset and dispersion but can shorten duration and increase systemic absorption)
Furosemide, benzodiazepines, phenytoin (incompatible - may be inactivated or precipitate; do not mix)
interactions.diagnostics: Heparin and certain ions can inhibit enzyme activity in vitro; intravenous administration leads to rapid inactivation.

rare: Ocular damage if applied to the eye

counsel: This enzyme is injected to help fluids or another medicine spread and absorb more quickly under the skin
Tell staff right away about any rash, itching, swelling, or difficulty breathing after the injection
Mild redness or swelling at the injection site is common and usually settles
It is also used by clinicians to treat fluid that has leaked from a drip and to dissolve certain cosmetic fillers
pk: Acts almost immediately at the injection site to increase tissue permeability
Maximal local spreading effect within minutes of injection

pearls: A 'spreading factor' - temporarily breaks down hyaluronic acid to disperse co-injected fluids and drugs
Mainstay off-label antidote for many drug and contrast extravasations - give early, infiltrating around the site
Used to dissolve hyaluronic acid dermal fillers, including vascular-occlusion emergencies
Never inject into infected/inflamed tissue (can spread infection) or onto the cornea
Rapidly inactivated if given intravenously - it is a local/subcutaneous agent
missed: Not applicable; hyaluronidase is given by a clinician as a single adjuvant injection for a specific procedure, not on a regular dosing schedule.
overdose: Overdose is uncommon given local use; excessive use could increase local tissue permeability and the systemic absorption of co-injected drugs. Management is supportive, with treatment of any hypersensitivity reaction and observation for effects of any co-administered agent.
